one_month_reasoning: I accept the supervisor's finding that Q3 2026 results most likely come on Wednesday 2026-11-04. Materion has reported Q3 exactly 33 days after quarter end every year from 2022 to 2025, the fiscal Q3 ends Oct 2, and MarketBeat estimates Nov 4. That is after the 1-month close (Fri 2026-10-30, since Nov 1 is a Sunday), so my round-1 Oct 28 date and its earnings jump are removed. The window holds only the date announcement and peer reads (semicap and connector earnings in late October). With no scheduled company event I stay close to a symmetric lognormal: median ~$309, a small give-back of the unexplained +16% Oct 1-2 spike (no 8-K, and Jefferies' $314 initiation was already out by Sep 2), with sigma 15.5% over the month. That sits a little under 59%/3.5 = 16.9% because earnings are out of the window, but not far under, given the stock's 2026 swings (-36% in one month with no news, then a +30.8% day). The base-rate tilt from short-term reversal after a sharp 2-day spike is offset by 52-week-high momentum, so I don't add a directional view.

fair_value.method: A blend of three methods. P/E: 2028E EPS $9.72 (FY2027 consensus $8.45 x 1.15) x 29x = $282, weight 0.5. Historical reversion: $9.72 x 22x = $214, weight 0.2. EV/EBITDA: 2028E adjusted EBITDA $360M x 19x = $6.84B, less ~$360M horizon net debt, over 21.1M diluted shares = $307, weight 0.3. Blended 12-month fair value is about $276.

bear.story: The theme unwinds, as in 2007-08, 2011 and Jul 2026 (-36% in one month without an earnings miss). A semis/AI capex digestion or a 2027 recession (Kalshi 23%) trims 2027 EPS to ~$8, and the multiple falls toward the 22x historical midpoint.

base.story: 2027 EPS of ~$8.45 is met, growth heads toward mid-teens into 2028, and the multiple compresses from ~37x FY2027 to ~29-30x NTM, near the bottom of the peer range, so the price ends slightly below today's spike.

bull.story: Beat-and-raise into 2027 (EPS above $9.3), the defense beryllium ramp and a critical-minerals scarcity premium hold the multiple near the top of the peer range (35-40x, ENTG/HWM/ROG levels) on 2028E of ~$10.5-11.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $185 the stock would be under the 2026-07-29 closing low ($189.34) and below ~22x FY2027 consensus EPS of ~$8.45, MTRN's own historical midpoint. The whole 2026 re-rating would have unwound and the post-print support at ~$230 (Aug 24) would have failed. That would most likely mean estimates are being cut (semis/AI digestion, defense slippage, a lower 2027 guide in Jan-Feb) rather than ordinary 55-60% volatility.

reasoning: Base-rate lens, revised for the supervisor's fact-checks. Corrections: the July 2026 fall (-36% from Jun 30 to Jul 29) came with no earnings release, and the Aug 5 beat-and-raise gave +30.8%. Guidance was raised once, not for three quarters. FY2027 consensus is ~$8.45, not ~$7.9. Use 21.1M diluted shares and $420.7M company net debt. Q3 is most likely Nov 4, outside the 1-month window. The July episode is itself a base rate: a theme drawdown with no fundamental trigger, which the stock fully recovered. That supports the supervisor's point that my round-1 25% bear scenario plus a 15% crash component double-counted the downside, so I cut the crash component to 10% and raised the main lognormal median from $295 to $300 (sigma 0.47). Fair value rises from $265 to $276, mostly because of the higher EPS base ($8.45 vs $8.40 and $9.72 vs $9.80 2028E roughly offset) and the peer-informed multiples (29x vs 28x, the peer median; the EV/EBITDA leg now values 2028E on diluted shares and a lower horizon net debt). Comps (11 peers) put MTRN at 37-39x forward EPS against a 29x peer median, with lower consensus growth (20% vs 24%) and ROIC (8.3% vs 10.1%), so I value it at the peer median. Old-economy base rates (MTRN 2008, 2011) and momentum-crash evidence argue for de-rating, and 52-week-high momentum and the beat history argue against it. The resulting distribution has a median of ~$283, P(>= $312) of 42.5% and a fat right tail (P(>= $468) 15.5%). It sits below spot because the expected return relies on EPS outrunning de-rating. Research this round was limited to peer statistics and forecast pages; I did not re-verify the supervisor's EDGAR checks and accept them as evidenced.

comps_summary.peer_set_note: 11 peers: four A&D specialty materials (CRS, ATI, HWM, HXL), six semiconductor/electronics materials and supply chain (ENTG, MKSI, UCTT, ESI, ROG, AMKR) and one metal pass-through processor (KALU), matching MTRN's semis ~54% / A&D ~20% of value-added sales mix. MP Materials was considered and excluded: forward P/E 114x and EV/EBITDA 194x on near-zero earnings (StockAnalysis), so it is not a meaningful multiple comparable. No other listed beryllium or precious-metal-target producer is US-listed.
comps_summary.peer_median_quality: ROIC 10.1%, EBITDA margin 19.4% of sales, debt/EBITDA 2.33x, beta 1.26 (StockAnalysis statistics pages)
comps_summary.mtrn_today: MTRN today: 39.4x forward P/E (StockAnalysis) and ~37x FY2027 consensus EPS of $8.43-8.48, a ~35% premium to the 29.0x peer median while its FY2027 EPS growth (+20.1%) is below the peer median (+24.3%). Its ROIC is 8.3% vs 10.1%, its EBITDA margin 9.8% of net sales (pass-through-inflated) vs 19.4%, debt/EBITDA 2.32x vs 2.33x, and beta 1.06 vs 1.26. The estimated forward EV/EBITDA on the same method is ~25.5x (34.04/1.334), above the ~19.3x median, and ~21x on my 2027E adjusted EBITDA.
comps_summary.mtrn_in_methods: Main P/E leg: 29x NTM EPS at the horizon, equal to the 29.0x peer median and inside the range. Base-rate leg: 22x (weight 0.2), inside the peer range and below the median. EV/EBITDA leg: 19x NTM adjusted EBITDA, at the ~19.3x peer median and inside the range. Weighted, the P/E legs imply ~27x (0.5x29 + 0.2x22 over 0.7), a ~7% discount to the median.
comps_summary.justification: I do not give MTRN today's ~35% premium to the peer median, because none of the persistent factors supports it. Growth: consensus FY2027 EPS growth of 20% is below the peer median of 24%, and MTRN's EPS was flat from 2022 to 2025 before 2026. Returns on capital: ROIC is 8.3% against a 10.1% median and far below the A&D leaders CRS (22%) and HWM (23%). Margins: EBITDA is 9.8% of net sales because of pass-through metal; even on value-added sales (23.3% in Q2 2026) it only matches the median and includes one-time items. Cyclicality: realized volatility is 59% and the stock fell -36% in July 2026 with no earnings news, with similar earlier crashes in 2008 and 2011. Balance sheet: leverage is at the median (2.32x vs 2.33x), neutral. The only structural positive is the defense-funded beryllium position (sole Western supplier, $65M customer-funded expansion). That argues against a discount to the median, so the main leg sits at the median rather than below it. The small blended discount comes only from the 0.2-weight base-rate leg, which reflects MTRN's own lower-ROIC, lower-growth history; sell-side outperformance calls play no part.
